rows: What does "seed spice" actually mean botanically?
Schizocarp (split fruit with 2 mericarps), not true seeds
Why does cilantro taste like soap to some people?
OR6A2 olfactory receptor variant → preferential binding to (E)-2-aldehydes → "soapy" perception. ~4–14% of people.
Trans-anethole — appears in fennel, anise, star anise, and licorice despite these being unrelated plants
R-carvone (caraway) and S-carvone (spearmint) are enantiomers — mirror images. Same formula, completely different smell because olfactory receptors are chiral proteins.
Nigella sativa — completely different family (Ranunculaceae). Not related to cumin. Active compound: thymoquinone, not cuminaldehyde.
Why does Florence fennel (bulb) taste different from fennel seed?
Different plant part, different compound ratios. Bulb = milder, sweeter. Seed = concentrated anethole.
Why do anethole liquors (pastis, ouzo, arak) go cloudy with water?
Anethole is hydrophobic. When ethanol concentration drops (dilution with water), anethole precipitates as tiny droplets → louche (milky emulsion). "Ouzo effect."
